propositions: Three top-level CLI verbs (bridge-fsck, bridge-probe, jira-onboard) must be renamed to noun-based forms nested under a bridge command group (bridge fsck, bridge check-access, bridge setup) while preserving old spellings as compatibility entrypoints.

The new bridge noun group must have three child commands registered in _bridge_commands.py that dispatch to existing implementations without behavioral changes: fsck and check-access as nested verbs, and setup as a pass-through to the jira-onboard wizard.

All JSON schema documents, help text files, CLI dispatch arms, generated references, tests, and documentation must be updated to use the canonical new spellings while allowing old spellings to remain executable.

The bridge-probe command shall be renamed to bridge check-access as its own primary verb (not a flag), creating and deleting a real Jira issue for access validation, distinct from the read-only fsck audit.

String-based test assertions and monkeypatched symbol references to old verb names must be updated across unit tests, integration tests, and reference generators through explicit grep validation to ensure no stale uses remain outside approved allowlists.

The canary bridge scripts and GitHub workflows must invoke the new verb names, output schema $id and description fields must reflect the new canonical spellings, and parity tests must verify both old and new spellings preserve exit codes, output, and behavior.
